chapter: Original Dixieland Jazz Band: Chicago and New York
title: How Shields replaced Nunes on clarinet
summary: Shields, idle in Chicago, is lined up to replace Nunes the next time he quits.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Who was the clarinet between Shields and Nunes, if any? Was there anybody in between? Nobody?

Shields joined at, Shields had been around Chicago and he hadn't been doing anything. And we saw him. And I asked him, how would you like to come with us? Geez, I wish I could. I said, well, I think we'll be able to make it because Nunes, every once in a while, he quits. Comes in late. Quits. He thinks he can't get anyone else. And he believes that he has the upper hand. So, the next time he quits, which will be in a few days, because he does it almost nightly. He will call you up and you come right down. So, he did. And Shields was with us then on. That was about, at the Casino Gardens around, and then on. It was early summer. June of July, 1916. So, March, April, May, June. Yes. June of July, 1916. July, most likely.
